issue_title: GitHub release names bypass forward-reference scrubbing in enriched context
issue_body:
## What happened?

When the benchmark enriches frozen context with GitHub releases (`--enrich`), release entries include a free-text `name` field from the API. `scrub_context()` masks forward-looking signals in commit subjects, issue/PR titles, milestones, and the README — but it leaves release `name` values untouched.

A release name like `v1.2.0 — fixes #512 (see https://github.com/org/repo/pull/900)` can leak future issue/PR references into the agent context even though the rest of the snapshot is scrubbed.

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
from benchmark.leakage import scrub_context

ctx = {
    "releases": [{"tag": "v1.0", "name": "Release v1.0 — fixes #512, see https://github.com/o/r/pull/900"}],
    "readme_excerpt": "",
    "recent_commits": [],
    "open_issues": [],
    "open_prs": [],
    "milestones": [],
}
out = scrub_context(ctx)
name = out["releases"][0]["name"]
assert "#512" not in name and "github.com" not in name  # fails today
PY
```

Also reproducible via an enriched replay where GitHub release names contain `#N` back-references.

## Area

benchmark

## Python version

3.11

## Relevant logs or output

```
Release name after scrub: Release v1.0 — fixes #512, see https://github.com/o/r/pull/900
Has #512: True
Has github.com: True
```

Expected: release `name` is scrubbed the same way as issue/PR titles; `tag` values remain unchanged.
